# Yop2D, full guide for AI assistants

> Read this file before answering a question about Yop2D. It explains how the engine thinks, the mistakes people (and AIs) make most often, and ends with the list of every node. A shorter summary is at https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/llms.txt.

## How to answer a Yop2D user

- **Never answer "this is not possible in Yop2D" before reading the sections "Which tool for which need" and "Frequent mistakes" below.** Many things that look impossible have a ready solution there (for example using objects of another scene, see below). If you still find no way, say you are not sure and suggest the Yop2D Discord instead of saying it is impossible.
- Yop2D is a **no-code** 2D game engine for Android. Users build games by touching and connecting **nodes** (a visual script called the **Blueprint**). **Never write programming code** (no Java, no Python, no Unity or Godot code). Give numbered steps using the exact names of buttons, nodes and settings.
- **Use only the nodes listed at the end of this file.** Never invent a node, a setting or a button. If you are not sure something exists, say so and suggest asking on the Yop2D Discord.
- Node names change with the interface language. The list below uses the English names; the table "Node names in every language" at the end gives the exact name in the 8 other languages. **Reply in the user's language and copy the node names from that table: never translate a name yourself.** The names of a node's settings and exits (for example "Loaded" / "No save found") are also translated in the app: for them, point the user to the node reference in their language (https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/noeuds/<lang>.html, lang = fr, es, de, it, pt, ru, zh, ja) or tell them to read the names shown in the node window; do not leave English words in a French, Spanish or German answer. Do not confuse "Go to a point (path)" / "Go to an object (path)" (automatic pathfinding) with "Follow the path" (a hand-made path from the Assets Path editor). Do not assume the user has the newest version: the version they tell you decides which nodes exist.
- Some nodes are marked **[newer than 1.0.1142]**: they are NOT in the public Google Play version (which is 1.0.1142), only in the Discord test versions. **Version rule: the Google Play version is 1.0.1142. Any version number ABOVE 1142 (for example 1.0.1232) is a test version and DOES contain all the nodes marked [newer than 1.0.1142].** So if the user says their version is higher than 1142, offer those nodes first (for example Path editor + "Follow the path", or "Play movement (steps)") and never say that the version is the Google Play one. If the version is 1142 or lower, say the node needs an update or the test version, and give the alternative.
- The user is usually a beginner on a **phone or tablet** (touch screen, no mouse). Keep answers short and simple. Do not use jargon without explaining it.
- Ask for what you need: the Yop2D version (start screen), which scene the node is in, the exact settings of the node, and what they expected versus what happens. The best thing a user can paste is the text of their Blueprint: in the Blueprint, the `{ }` button shows the nodes of the current scene as text.
- Always suggest the built-in checks when something does not work: **menu ☰ → Check my game** (lists missing variables, objects, files and unconnected nodes), and the detailed log (start screen → 🐞 button → tick "detailed log", play, then Copy).
- If the question is about making a whole kind of game, point to the matching guide (list below) before improvising.

## The most used node names, in every language (about 140 nodes)

Copy these names exactly. Do NOT add or change small words (for example the French name is "Sauvegarder les variables dans un fichier", not "Sauvegarder des variables…"; "Ajouter à Variable", not "Ajouter à la variable"). In French the word is "nœud" (not "node"). The full table is at the end of this file.

- **On Start** → fr: Au Démarrage | es: Al Iniciar | de: Beim Start | it: All'Avvio | pt: Ao Iniciar | ru: При старте | zh: 启动时 | ja: 起動時
- **Every frame** → fr: À chaque image | es: Cada fotograma | de: Jeden Frame | it: Ogni frame | pt: A cada frame | ru: Каждый кадр | zh: 每帧 | ja: 毎フレーム
- **On Object Click** → fr: Au Clic sur Objet | es: Al Clic en Objeto | de: Bei Objektklick | it: Al Clic sull'Oggetto | pt: Ao Clicar no Objeto | ru: Клик по объекту | zh: 点击对象时 | ja: オブジェクトクリック時
- **If object touches Tag** → fr: Si objet touche Tag | es: Si el objeto toca el Tag | de: Wenn Objekt Tag berührt | it: Se l'oggetto tocca il Tag | pt: Se o objeto tocar no Tag | ru: Если объект касается тега | zh: 如果对象碰到标签 | ja: オブジェクトがタグに触れた場合
- **Collision A/B** → fr: Collision A/B | es: Colisión A/B | de: Kollision A/B | it: Collisione A/B | pt: Colisão A/B | ru: Столкновение A/B | zh: 碰撞 A/B | ja: 衝突 A/B
- **Back button pressed** → fr: Bouton retour pressé | es: Botón atrás pulsado | de: Zurück-Taste gedrückt | it: Tasto indietro premuto | pt: Botão voltar pressionado | ru: Нажата кнопка «Назад» | zh: 按下返回键 | ja: 戻るボタンを押したとき
- **Move Object** → fr: Déplacer Objet | es: Mover Objeto | de: Objekt bewegen | it: Sposta Oggetto | pt: Mover Objeto | ru: Переместить | zh: 移动对象 | ja: オブジェクトを移動
- **Push object** → fr: Pousser objet | es: Empujar objeto | de: Objekt schieben | it: Spingi l'oggetto | pt: Empurrar objeto | ru: Толкнуть объект | zh: 推动对象 | ja: オブジェクトを押す
- **Set a property** → fr: Modifier une propriété | es: Modificar una propiedad | de: Eigenschaft ändern | it: Modifica una proprietà | pt: Modificar uma propriedade | ru: Изменить свойство | zh: 修改属性 | ja: プロパティを変更
- **Destroy Object** → fr: Détruire Objet | es: Destruir Objeto | de: Objekt zerstören | it: Distruggi Oggetto | pt: Destruir Objeto | ru: Уничтожить объект | zh: 销毁对象 | ja: オブジェクトを破壊
- **Give a tag (object family)** → fr: Donner un tag (famille d'objets) | es: Dar una etiqueta (familia de objetos) | de: Tag geben (Objektfamilie) | it: Dare un tag (famiglia di oggetti) | pt: Dar uma tag (família de objetos) | ru: Присвоить тег (семейство объектов) | zh: 设置标签（对象分组） | ja: タグをつける（オブジェクトの仲間）
- **Create a copy of the object** → fr: Créer une copie de l'objet | es: Crear una copia del objeto | de: Eine Kopie des Objekts erstellen | it: Crea una copia dell'oggetto | pt: Criar uma cópia do objeto | ru: Создать копию объекта | zh: 创建对象的副本 | ja: オブジェクトのコピーを作る
- **Shoot an object** → fr: Tirer un objet | es: Disparar un objeto | de: Ein Objekt abfeuern | it: Spara un oggetto | pt: Disparar um objeto | ru: Стрелять объектом | zh: 发射对象 | ja: オブジェクトを発射
- **Add to Variable** → fr: Ajouter à Variable | es: Añadir a Variable | de: Zu Variable hinzufügen | it: Aggiungi alla Variabile | pt: Adicionar à Variável | ru: Добавить к переменной | zh: 增加变量值 | ja: 変数に加算
- **Modify Variable** → fr: Modifier Variable | es: Modificar Variable | de: Variable ändern | it: Modifica Variabile | pt: Modificar Variável | ru: Изменить переменную | zh: 修改变量 | ja: 変数を変更
- **Condition** → fr: Condition | es: Condición | de: Bedingung | it: Condizione | pt: Condição | ru: Условие | zh: 条件 | ja: 条件
- **If / Else** → fr: Si / Sinon | es: Si / Si no | de: Wenn / Sonst | it: Se / Altrimenti | pt: Se / Senão | ru: Если / Иначе | zh: 如果 / 否则 | ja: もし / それ以外
- **Wait** → fr: Attendre | es: Esperar | de: Warten | it: Attendere | pt: Esperar | ru: Ждать | zh: 等待 | ja: 待つ
- **Repeat** → fr: Répéter | es: Repetir | de: Wiederholen | it: Ripetere | pt: Repetir | ru: Повторять | zh: 重复 | ja: 繰り返す
- **Modify Text** → fr: Modifier Texte | es: Modificar Texto | de: Text ändern | it: Modifica Testo | pt: Modificar Texto | ru: Изменить текст | zh: 修改文本 | ja: テキストを変更
- **Play sound** → fr: Jouer un son | es: Reproducir sonido | de: Sound abspielen | it: Riproduci suono | pt: Tocar som | ru: Воспроизвести звук | zh: 播放音效 | ja: 効果音を再生
- **Play music** → fr: Jouer la musique | es: Reproducir música | de: Musik abspielen | it: Riproduci musica | pt: Tocar música | ru: Включить музыку | zh: 播放音乐 | ja: 音楽を再生
- **Go to scene** → fr: Changer de scène | es: Ir a la escena | de: Zur Szene wechseln | it: Vai alla scena | pt: Ir para a cena | ru: Перейти к сцене | zh: 切换场景 | ja: シーンを切り替える
- **Restart the scene** → fr: Recommencer la scène | es: Reiniciar la escena | de: Szene neu starten | it: Ricomincia la scena | pt: Reiniciar a cena | ru: Перезапустить сцену | zh: 重新开始场景 | ja: シーンをやり直す
- **Follow with camera** → fr: Fixer la caméra | es: Fijar la cámara | de: Kamera fixieren | it: Fissa la camera | pt: Fixar a câmera | ru: Закрепить камеру | zh: 锁定相机 | ja: カメラを固定
- **Glide to** → fr: Glisser vers | es: Deslizar hacia | de: Gleiten nach | it: Scivola verso | pt: Deslizar para | ru: Скользить к | zh: 滑向 | ja: スライド移動
- **Chase an object** → fr: Poursuivre un objet | es: Perseguir un objeto | de: Objekt verfolgen | it: Insegui un oggetto | pt: Perseguir um objeto | ru: Преследовать | zh: 追踪对象 | ja: オブジェクトを追跡
- **Play animation** → fr: Jouer l'animation | es: Reproducir animación | de: Animation abspielen | it: Riproduci animazione | pt: Reproduzir animação | ru: Запустить анимацию | zh: 播放动画 | ja: アニメを再生
- **Save variables to a file** → fr: Sauvegarder les variables dans un fichier | es: Guardar variables en un archivo | de: Variablen in einer Datei speichern | it: Salva le variabili in un file | pt: Salvar variáveis em um arquivo | ru: Сохранить переменные в файл | zh: 把变量保存到文件 | ja: 変数をファイルに保存
- **Load variables from a file** → fr: Charger les variables depuis un fichier | es: Cargar variables desde un archivo | de: Variablen aus einer Datei laden | it: Carica le variabili da un file | pt: Carregar variáveis de um arquivo | ru: Загрузить переменные из файла | zh: 从文件加载变量 | ja: ファイルから変数を読み込む
- **Show dialogue** → fr: Afficher un dialogue | es: Mostrar diálogo | de: Dialog anzeigen | it: Mostra dialogo | pt: Mostrar diálogo | ru: Показать диалог | zh: 显示对话 | ja: ダイアログを表示
- **Say a line** → fr: Dire une phrase | es: Decir una frase | de: Einen Satz sagen | it: Dire una frase | pt: Dizer uma frase | ru: Сказать фразу | zh: 说一句话 | ja: セリフを言う
- **Ask a choice** → fr: Poser un choix | es: Proponer una elección | de: Eine Wahl stellen | it: Proporre una scelta | pt: Propor uma escolha | ru: Предложить выбор | zh: 提出选择 | ja: 選択肢を出す
- **Run one of my nodes** → fr: Lancer un de mes nœuds | es: Usar uno de mis nodos | de: Einen meiner Knoten starten | it: Avvia uno dei miei nodi | pt: Usar um dos meus nós | ru: Запустить один из моих узлов | zh: 运行我的节点 | ja: マイノードを実行
- **Call event** → fr: Appeler un événement | es: Llamar evento | de: Ereignis aufrufen | it: Chiama evento | pt: Chamar evento | ru: Вызвать событие | zh: 调用事件 | ja: イベントを呼ぶ
- **Local Event** → fr: Événement Local | es: Evento Local | de: Lokales Ereignis | it: Evento Locale | pt: Evento Local | ru: Локальное событие | zh: 本地事件 | ja: ローカルイベント
- **Follow the path** → fr: Suivre le parcours | es: Seguir el recorrido | de: Dem Weg folgen | it: Seguire il percorso | pt: Seguir o percurso | ru: Идти по маршруту | zh: 沿路线前进 | ja: ルートをたどる
- **Play movement (steps)** → fr: Jouer le mouvement (étapes) | es: Reproducir movimiento (etapas) | de: Bewegung abspielen (Etappen) | it: Riprodurre il movimento (tappe) | pt: Reproduzir movimento (etapas) | ru: Запустить движение (этапы) | zh: 播放动作（步骤） | ja: 動きを再生（ステップ）
- **Stop the movement** → fr: Arrêter le mouvement | es: Detener el movimiento | de: Bewegung stoppen | it: Fermare il movimento | pt: Parar o movimento | ru: Остановить движение | zh: 停止动作 | ja: 動きを止める
- **Stop following the path** → fr: Arrêter le parcours | es: Detener el recorrido | de: Weg abbrechen | it: Fermare il percorso | pt: Parar o percurso | ru: Остановить маршрут | zh: 停止路线 | ja: ルートをやめる
- **Spin the object continuously** → fr: Faire tourner l'objet en continu | es: Hacer girar el objeto sin parar | de: Objekt ununterbrochen drehen | it: Far girare l'oggetto di continuo | pt: Girar o objeto sem parar | ru: Непрерывно вращать объект | zh: 让对象持续旋转 | ja: オブジェクトをずっと回す
- **Flee an object** → fr: Fuir un objet | es: Huir de un objeto | de: Vor Objekt fliehen | it: Fuggi da un oggetto | pt: Fugir de um objeto | ru: Убегать | zh: 躲避对象 | ja: オブジェクトから逃げる
- **Go to an object (path)** → fr: Aller vers un objet (chemin) | es: Ir hacia un objeto (camino) | de: Zu einem Objekt gehen (Weg) | it: Andare verso un oggetto (percorso) | pt: Ir até um objeto (caminho) | ru: Идти к объекту (путь) | zh: 走向对象（寻路） | ja: オブジェクトへ行く（道さがし）
- **Go to a point (path)** → fr: Aller à un point (chemin) | es: Ir a un punto (camino) | de: Zu einem Punkt gehen (Weg) | it: Andare a un punto (percorso) | pt: Ir até um ponto (caminho) | ru: Идти к точке (путь) | zh: 走到某个点（寻路） | ja: 場所へ行く（道さがし）
- **Stop the path** → fr: Arrêter le chemin | es: Detener el camino | de: Weg stoppen | it: Fermare il percorso | pt: Parar o caminho | ru: Остановить путь | zh: 停止寻路 | ja: 道さがしを止める
- **Place on a cell (column, row)** → fr: Placer sur une case (colonne, ligne) | es: Colocar en una casilla (columna, fila) | de: Auf ein Feld setzen (Spalte, Zeile) | it: Mettere su una casella (colonna, riga) | pt: Colocar em uma casa (coluna, linha) | ru: Поставить на клетку (столбец, строка) | zh: 放到某个格子（列，行） | ja: マスに置く（列、行）
- **Go to the cell (path)** → fr: Aller à la case (chemin) | es: Ir a la casilla (camino) | de: Zum Feld gehen (Weg) | it: Vai alla casella (percorso) | pt: Ir para a casa (caminho) | ru: Идти к клетке (путь) | zh: 走到格子（寻路） | ja: マスへ行く（道）
- **Change the behavior** → fr: Changer le comportement | es: Cambiar el comportamiento | de: Verhalten ändern | it: Cambia il comportamento | pt: Mudar o comportamento | ru: Изменить поведение | zh: 改变行为 | ja: ふるまいを変える
- **Show reachable cells** → fr: Montrer les cases accessibles | es: Mostrar casillas accesibles | de: Erreichbare Felder zeigen | it: Mostra le caselle raggiungibili | pt: Mostrar casas alcançáveis | ru: Показать доступные клетки | zh: 显示可到达的格子 | ja: 行けるマスを表示
- **Hide the cells** → fr: Cacher les cases | es: Ocultar las casillas | de: Felder verbergen | it: Nascondi le caselle | pt: Esconder as casas | ru: Скрыть клетки | zh: 隐藏格子 | ja: マスを隠す
- **If the cell is reachable** → fr: Si la case est accessible | es: Si la casilla es accesible | de: Wenn das Feld erreichbar ist | it: Se la casella è raggiungibile | pt: Se a casa for alcançável | ru: Если клетка доступна | zh: 如果格子可到达 | ja: もしマスに行けるなら
- **Give a unit sheet** → fr: Donner une fiche d'unité | es: Dar una ficha de unidad | de: Einheitenblatt geben | it: Dai una scheda unità | pt: Dar uma ficha de unidade | ru: Дать карточку юнита | zh: 给单位卡 | ja: ユニットカードをあたえる
- **Attack** → fr: Attaquer | es: Atacar | de: Angreifen | it: Attacca | pt: Atacar | ru: Атаковать | zh: 攻击 | ja: こうげきする

- **Go to the next turn** → fr: Passer au tour suivant | es: Pasar al siguiente turno | de: Zum nächsten Zug | it: Passa al turno successivo | pt: Passar para o próximo turno | ru: Перейти к следующему ходу | zh: 进入下一回合 | ja: 次のターンへ

- **Select the object** → fr: Sélectionner l'objet | es: Seleccionar el objeto | de: Objekt auswählen | it: Seleziona l'oggetto | pt: Selecionar o objeto | ru: Выбрать объект | zh: 选中对象 | ja: オブジェクトを選ぶ

- **Destroy by Tag** → fr: Détruire par Tag | es: Destruir por Tag | de: Zerstören nach Tag | it: Distruggi tramite Tag | pt: Destruir por Tag | ru: Уничтожить по тегу | zh: 按标签销毁 | ja: タグで破壊

- **Random number** → fr: Nombre aléatoire | es: Número aleatorio | de: Zufallszahl | it: Numero casuale | pt: Número aleatório | ru: Случайное число | zh: 随机数 | ja: ランダムな数

- **If joystick** → fr: Si joystick | es: Si joystick | de: Wenn Joystick | it: Se joystick | pt: Se joystick | ru: Если джойстик | zh: 如果摇杆 | ja: ジョイスティックが
- **If on ground** → fr: Si au sol | es: Si está en el suelo | de: Wenn am Boden | it: Se è a terra | pt: Se está no chão | ru: Если на земле | zh: 如果在地面 | ja: 地面にいるなら
- **If off-screen** → fr: Si hors écran | es: Si fuera de pantalla | de: Wenn außerhalb des Bildschirms | it: Se fuori schermo | pt: Se fora da tela | ru: Если за пределами экрана | zh: 如果在屏幕外 | ja: 画面外にいるなら

## The big picture

- A **project** contains one or more **scenes** (levels, menus). A special scene called a **HUD** can be shown over a game scene for score, buttons and joystick. The start scene is the first one in the Scenes list (the star marks it).
- A scene contains **objects**. Each object has a **name** and optionally a **tag**. In the editor, the left panel lists the objects (Hierarchy), the canvas shows the scene, the right panel (Inspector) shows the settings of the selected object. The top bar has: Object (add), Save, Undo, Redo, Copy, Delete, Move, Hand, Grid, Center, Zoom, Blueprint, Help, Menu, Play. On a phone some of these are in a menu.
- **Play** runs the game; the stop button returns to the editor. Saving is automatic (every minute by default), and the 💾 button saves now.
- Objects: image, text, shapes (square, circle…), zone (invisible area, can have several points), joystick, buttons, particles, tile layer ("tile scenery"), scene instance (a scene placed inside another = a **prefab**), and interface elements (button, switch, checkbox, slider, panel, counter).
- **Assets**: images, sounds, fonts, texts live in the project. The **Yop2D Library** has ready images (with animations), sounds, music, fonts, titles. Free packs, prefabs and examples can be downloaded from the Library and the Examples tab.
- The editor has small tools in the Assets window: Music, Sound effect, Movement (animation by steps), Parcours (paths for enemies), Sheet (cut a sprite sheet), Character, Animations, Titles, Start screen.

## Objects, inspector, behaviors

- Inspector fields: name, ⚙ **Behavior**, position, size, scale, rotation, Z (front/back: a higher Z is drawn in front), color, opacity, visible, shadow under the object, **Tag**, object variables, invisible touch area, parent, parallax, contact area (a custom area used for collisions).
- **Tags**: one object can have several tags. **Separate them with commas** (`enemy, danger`), never with spaces. A tag is a family name: one setup works for every object with that tag.
- **Behavior** (⚙ in the inspector) says how an object moves, with no nodes: Scenery (nothing), **Ground / wall** (does not move, you walk on it), Falls and bounces, **Platform character** (walks, jumps, climbs ladders; needs a joystick or buttons, and a jump button), **Patrol (back and forth)** (walks alone, turns at edges: for enemies), Top-down character, Dragged with a finger, **Elevator**, **Realistic physics**. An object can also be a ladder, traversable, pickable, drawn in front/behind by position. **Nodes always win**: if a node moves an object, it overrides the behavior.
- A joystick object has an **object to move** setting: pick the character in the inspector of the joystick.
- Text on a button: a text object must be a **child** of the button (parent) or share its tag, otherwise the text object captures the touch.
- A text drawn behind a panel is invisible: give the text a higher **Z** than the panel.
- Position coordinates are in game pixels. The default game is 1920 x 1080 (landscape) or 1080 x 1920 (portrait); the screen adaptation (keep shape / stretch / fill) is in Menu → Game settings.

## Variables and formulas

- **Variables** are created in the left panel (section Variables) with a type (integer, text, yes/no, list) and a scope: **local** (this scene, reset when the scene restarts) or **global** (whole game). **Object variables** belong to one object and are read with `objectname.variable`.
- Any numeric or text setting can be a **formula**, written with `=` in front: `=score + 1`, `="Score: " + score`, `=score >= 3`. Beginners should only use: a variable name, a simple comparison, a sum, a text. Do not suggest `&&`, `||`, nested parentheses or code-like functions.
- Handy values: `doigt.x`, `doigt.y` (finger position on screen), `joystick.x`, `joystick.y`, `ecran.largeur`, `ecran.hauteur`, `camera.x`, `camera.y`, `temps`, `langue_telephone`, `fps`, `delta`, `objectname.x`, `objectname.y`, `objectname.largeur`, `objectname.vitesse`. Functions: `random(a, b)`, `distance(a, b)`, `angle(a, b)`, `round`, `floor`, `ceil`, `abs`, `min`, `max`, `clamp`, `reste(a, b)`, `si(condition, a, b)`. The settings window has a left panel with these ready to tap, and a line "In plain words" that explains the formula.
- **Green nodes** ("value nodes": random number, object value, variable value, calculation, distance, touched column…) can be plugged into a setting with the 🔗 button instead of typing a formula.

## The Blueprint (nodes)

- Open it with the **Blueprint** button. Nodes are boxes. **Events** (red, e.g. On Start, Every frame, On Object Click, If object touches Tag) start a chain. **Actions** are connected after them with wires: drag a wire from an output (right side) to the input of the next node. An **output accepts one wire; an input accepts many**. The "Next" output runs the next node. **Conditions** have True/False outputs.
- Touch a node's frame to open its **settings window**: ① On what? (which object), ② Settings. The left list inserts objects, variables, tags and values.
- Dropping a wire into empty space opens a list of nodes to add. The wand button tidies the nodes. The ⬚ button selects several nodes to copy, paste or delete. Note and frame tools add sticky notes and titled frames to explain the nodes.
- **"The involved object"** (in English; "L'objet impliqué" in French) is the other object in a touch or click event: for "If object touches Tag", it is the object that was touched. This is how one setup affects the right pearl, enemy or card. "The selected object" is the one chosen with the selection nodes.
- A node only works in the scene whose Blueprint contains it (the Blueprint button shows the scene name; the HUD has its own Blueprint, where button clicks must be). **But a node CAN act on objects of another scene** (for example the HUD from the game scene): use the global logic, a tag, or a global variable with the event "When Variable Changes" (details in "Frequent mistakes", item 9). There is also a **global logic** that runs in every scene (the first line of the scene list in the Blueprint) and **My nodes** (reusable nodes you build yourself, with settings).
- To react to a click on several objects, use the target `tag:name`. For several objects at once in touch events, put the same tag on all.
- Prefabs: objects inside a prefab are renamed when placed ("_2"), so formulas must not name them; read variables of the object the node targets.
- Dialogues and translations: `dialogues.txt` (Assets) holds `key = text` and `key.en = …`, `key.fr = …`; the "Show a dialogue" node reads them in the language of the phone or of a `langue` variable.
- A project opened in an **older** Yop2D loses nodes it does not know when saved. Update Yop2D before opening projects made with a newer version.

## Which tool for which need (answer with these, do not invent nodes)

Always use the exact node names of the node reference. A node marked `[newer than 1.0.1142]` is NOT in the Google Play version: say so and tell the user to update Yop2D (or use the alternative given here).

**Moving things**
- Enemy that walks by itself on a platform: behavior **Patrol (back and forth)** in the object's Behavior window. It turns around at the edge of the ground or at a wall. It has no pause and no fixed points.
- Go back and forth between two points WITH a pause at each end: **Play movement (steps)** `[newer than 1.0.1142]` with a movement made in the Assets "Movement" editor (each step has a duration; looping), or **Follow the path** `[newer than 1.0.1142]` with a path from the Assets "Path" editor (each point has a waiting time). On the Play Store version: "Glide to" point B, "Wait", "Glide to" point A, "Wait", then "Call event" with a "Local Event" that restarts the same chain (avoid a "Repeat" with a fixed time, it drifts when the pauses change).
- Enemy that chases the hero: **Chase an object**; flee: **Flee an object**. On a grid/maze (walls, obstacles): **Go to an object (path)**, NOT "Chase an object" (which goes in a straight line and gets stuck on walls). Put it once, under "On Start" or an event: the path is recalculated automatically each time the target changes cell, so do not relaunch it with "Repeat" or "Every frame". "Stop the path" stops it. Walls must be solid (solid tiles of a tile layer, or fixed physical objects). The official example "Maze chase" does exactly this.
- Move to the finger: **Glide to** with `=doigt.x` / `=doigt.y`.
- Moving platform / lift: behavior **Elevator (back and forth)** (Behavior window) or a movement (steps) on a Ground object with "Carries what stands on it".
- Bouncing ball without gravity: no ready behavior; use variables `vx` / `vy` with "Push object" and "Collision A/B" (see the guide "Breakout").
- Camera: **Follow with camera**, **Camera limits** (enlarge them when the level is longer!), **Scroll the camera with a finger**.

**Fighting and lives**
- Touching an enemy hurts: event **If object touches Tag**, then "Add to Variable" (`vies`, -1) and a Condition `=vies <= 0`.
- Health bar, damage, healing: **Give health to the object**, **Deal damage**, **Heal**; health is the object variable `vie`.
- Turn-based tactics on a grid: **Go to the next turn**, **Show reachable cells**, **Attack**, **Give a unit sheet**, **Choose a target**, **Play like a computer (AI)**. If the attack range/zone does not appear: check that the range number is not 0 or empty, that the minimum range is smaller than the range, that a "custom" shape has positions written, that the zone name is not the same as the movement zone (the second replaces the first), and that nothing calls **Hide the cells** right after.

**Using objects of another scene (HUD, other level)**
- Pick them with the Blueprint button that shows the scene name → "Global logic (all scenes)" (its object list contains every scene's objects), or give them a tag and target `# tag` from any scene, or share a global variable and react to it with the event "When Variable Changes". Never say it is impossible.

**Showing and saving things**
- Score or any number on screen: "Modify Text" / "Set a property" on a text with `="Score: " + score`.
- Keep the score after closing the game: **Save variables to a file** then **Load variables from a file** (not "Save state", which only lasts until the game is closed).
- Dialogues in several languages: `dialogues.txt` + **Show dialogue**.
- Story with choices (visual novel): **Say a line**, **Ask a choice**, **Change the background**, **Story title screen**.
- Day/night, torches, shadows: **Day and night cycle**, **Light source (torch, lantern…)**, **Shadow under the object** (or the Shadow checkbox in the Inspector) `[newer than 1.0.1142]`.

**Sound and effects**
- Music at start: event **On Start** → **Play music** (loop). Own music: Assets → Music editor. Own sound effects: Assets → "Sound FX" editor.
- Explosion, sparks, rain: **Particle effect**; screen shake: **Camera shake**; slow motion: **Game speed (slow motion)**.

**Recipes**
- **Collect items**: give items a tag (`piece`). Event "If object touches Tag" (object A = player, tag = piece) → "Destroy Object" on **the involved object** → "Add to Variable" (score, 1) → "Set a property" on a text with value `="Score: " + score`.
- **Win after N items**: Condition `=score >= N`, then show a text, "Wait", and "Restart the scene" or "Next scene".
- **Platformer**: ground and platforms have behavior Ground / wall; the hero has Platform character; joystick (object to move = hero) and a jump button.
- **Shoot**: **Shoot an object** with a model object; **Cooldown** limits the rate.
- **Next level**: one scene per level, an arrival zone, "Go to scene".
- **Reuse a set of nodes**: Resources → My nodes (then "Run one of my nodes", with settings).
- **Tower defense / paths**: **Follow the path** `[newer than 1.0.1142]` with a path that has a crossroads.

## Frequent mistakes to check first

1. Nothing happens: is the node connected to an event? Is the event in the Blueprint of the scene where the object is? (The HUD has its own.) Did the user save (💾)? Is the tag spelled the same everywhere (lowercase, no accent, commas between several)? Run "Check my game".
2. A button's text steals the touch: make it a child of the button.
3. A formula refers to an object by name but the object was renamed or is in a prefab: use the targeted object or a variable.
4. A character does not move: behavior chosen? Joystick object-to-move set? Jump button set?
5. Sprites look blurry: pixel art needs the "pixel art: sharp pixels" option in Game settings.
6. Wrong or missing node: the user may have an older Yop2D (check the [newer than …] marks).
7. A node is missing in the list on a school-mode device: School mode hides advanced nodes.
8. Music or sound does not play: the file must be in the project's Sounds; OGG is the safest format.
9. "How do I select an object that is in another scene (for example the HUD)?" The node list "On what?" only shows the objects of the scene whose Blueprint is open; the HUD has its own Blueprint and objects. Three ways: (a) in the Blueprint, tap the scene-name button at the top and choose "Global logic (all scenes)": there the list shows the objects of every scene, HUD included; (b) give the HUD object a tag (Inspector → "For nodes" part) and in the game scene choose the group Tags → "# tag" (tags of all scenes are listed); (c) cleanest: the game scene changes a global variable (for example `score`) and the HUD's own Blueprint uses the event "When Variable Changes" to update its text with `="Score: " + score` (global variables are shared by all scenes).
10. The joystick slides toward a corner, leaves the screen or stays there after release: the engine never moves a joystick by itself. Usual cause: the joystick is in the GAME scene while the camera follows the player, so it is a world object that drifts as the camera moves. Fix: put the joystick in an interface (HUD) scene (second scene, opened with the node "Open a HUD" at start); the templates "Following camera (top-down)" (exactly this case: top-down game, camera following the player, joystick in the HUD) and "Use a HUD" show how it is built (Templates tab on the start screen). Second cause: the joystick is draggable (behavior other than fixed / scenery, or a "make draggable" node applied to it): then dragging moves the object itself. The joystick must have the player (or the object to move) selected in its settings.

## Node names in every language

The user's Yop2D may be in any of 9 languages. When the user writes in another language, use the node names from this table and never translate a node name yourself. English name first, then the exact name in fr, es, de, it, pt, ru, zh, ja.

### Events

- **On Start** → fr: Au Démarrage | es: Al Iniciar | de: Beim Start | it: All'Avvio | pt: Ao Iniciar | ru: При старте | zh: 启动时 | ja: 起動時
- **Every frame** → fr: À chaque image | es: Cada fotograma | de: Jeden Frame | it: Ogni frame | pt: A cada frame | ru: Каждый кадр | zh: 每帧 | ja: 毎フレーム
- **End of Click** → fr: Fin de Clic | es: Fin de Clic | de: Ende des Klicks | it: Fine del Clic | pt: Fim de Clique | ru: Конец клика | zh: 点击结束 | ja: クリック終了
- **On Object Click** → fr: Au Clic sur Objet | es: Al Clic en Objeto | de: Bei Objektklick | it: Al Clic sull'Oggetto | pt: Ao Clicar no Objeto | ru: Клик по объекту | zh: 点击对象时 | ja: オブジェクトクリック時
- **Object Released** → fr: Fin de Clic sur Objet | es: Fin de Clic en Objeto | de: Klick auf Objekt beendet | it: Fine del Clic su Oggetto | pt: Fim do Clique no Objeto | ru: Конец клика по объекту | zh: 松开物体 | ja: オブジェクトを離した時
- **Object Held Down** → fr: Maintenu sur Objet | es: Objeto Mantenido Pulsado | de: Objekt gehalten | it: Oggetto Tenuto Premuto | pt: Objeto Mantido Pressionado | ru: Объект удерживается | zh: 按住物体 | ja: オブジェクトを押している間
- **Finger held down** → fr: Doigt appuyé | es: Dedo presionado | de: Finger gedrückt | it: Dito premuto | pt: Dedo pressionado | ru: Палец нажат | zh: 手指按住 | ja: 指で押している間
- **Back button pressed** → fr: Bouton retour pressé | es: Botón atrás pulsado | de: Zurück-Taste gedrückt | it: Tasto indietro premuto | pt: Botão voltar pressionado | ru: Нажата кнопка «Назад» | zh: 按下返回键 | ja: 戻るボタンを押したとき
- **On every new scene** → fr: À chaque nouvelle scène | es: En cada escena nueva | de: Bei jeder neuen Szene | it: A ogni nuova scena | pt: A cada nova cena | ru: При каждой новой сцене | zh: 每次进入新场景 | ja: 新しいシーンが始まるたび

- **Collision A/B** → fr: Collision A/B | es: Colisión A/B | de: Kollision A/B | it: Collisione A/B | pt: Colisão A/B | ru: Столкновение A/B | zh: 碰撞 A/B | ja: 衝突 A/B
- **Exit Zone** → fr: Sortie de zone | es: Salida de zona | de: Zone verlassen | it: Esci dalla Zona | pt: Saída de zona | ru: Выход из зоны | zh: 离开区域 | ja: ゾーンから出る
- **On Hover** → fr: Au Survol | es: Al Pasar por Encima | de: Beim Hovern | it: Al Passaggio del Mouse | pt: Ao Passar o Mouse | ru: Наведение мыши | zh: 鼠标悬停 | ja: ホバー時
- **End of Hover** → fr: Fin de Survol | es: Fin de Pasar por Encima | de: Hover Ende | it: Fine Passaggio del Mouse | pt: Fim de Passar o Mouse | ru: Конец наведения | zh: 悬停结束 | ja: ホバー終了
- **On Impact (Physics)** → fr: Au Choc (Physique) | es: Al Impacto (Física) | de: Bei Aufprall (Physik) | it: All'Impatto (Fisica) | pt: Ao Impacto (Física) | ru: Столкновение (Физика) | zh: 物理撞击 | ja: 物理的な衝突時

### Time

- **Wait** → fr: Attendre | es: Esperar | de: Warten | it: Attendere | pt: Esperar | ru: Ждать | zh: 等待 | ja: 待つ
- **Repeat** → fr: Répéter | es: Repetir | de: Wiederholen | it: Ripetere | pt: Repetir | ru: Повторять | zh: 重复 | ja: 繰り返す
- **Countdown** → fr: Compte à rebours | es: Cuenta atrás | de: Countdown | it: Conto alla rovescia | pt: Contagem regressiva | ru: Обратный отсчёт | zh: 倒计时 | ja: カウントダウン

- **Novel mode (full-screen text)** → fr: Mode roman (texte plein écran) | es: Modo novela (texto a pantalla completa) | de: Romanmodus (Text im Vollbild) | it: Modalità romanzo (testo a schermo intero) | pt: Modo romance (texto em tela cheia) | ru: Режим романа (текст на весь экран) | zh: 小说模式（全屏文字） | ja: ノベルモード（全画面テキスト）
- **SMS mode (phone conversation)** → fr: Mode SMS (conversation sur téléphone) | es: Modo SMS (conversación en el móvil) | de: SMS-Modus (Chat am Handy) | it: Modalità SMS (conversazione sul telefono) | pt: Modo SMS (conversa no celular) | ru: Режим SMS (переписка на телефоне) | zh: 短信模式（手机聊天） | ja: SMSモード（スマホで会話）
- **Unlock an achievement** → fr: Débloquer un succès | es: Desbloquear un logro | de: Erfolg freischalten | it: Sbloccare un obiettivo | pt: Desbloquear uma conquista | ru: Открыть достижение | zh: 解锁成就 | ja: 実績を解除する
- **Replayable scene (gallery)** → fr: Scène à rejouer (galerie) | es: Escena rejugable (galería) | de: Wiederholbare Szene (Galerie) | it: Scena da rigiocare (galleria) | pt: Cena para rever (galeria) | ru: Сцена для повтора (галерея) | zh: 可重播场景（画廊） | ja: リプレイできる場面（ギャラリー）
- **End the story** → fr: Terminer l'histoire | es: Terminar la historia | de: Geschichte beenden | it: Terminare la storia | pt: Terminar a história | ru: Завершить историю | zh: 结束故事 | ja: 物語を終える
- **Friendship (hearts)** → fr: Amitié (cœurs) | es: Amistad (corazones) | de: Freundschaft (Herzen) | it: Amicizia (cuori) | pt: Amizade (corações) | ru: Дружба (сердечки) | zh: 友情（爱心） | ja: 友情（ハート）
- **If the friendship…** → fr: Si l'amitié… | es: Si la amistad… | de: Wenn die Freundschaft… | it: Se l'amicizia… | pt: Se a amizade… | ru: Если дружба… | zh: 如果友情…… | ja: もし友情が…
- **Story title screen** → fr: Écran titre de l'histoire | es: Pantalla de título de la historia | de: Titelbildschirm der Geschichte | it: Schermata del titolo della storia | pt: Tela de título da história | ru: Титульный экран истории | zh: 故事标题画面 | ja: 物語のタイトル画面
- **Ask the player for a text (name…)** → fr: Demander un texte au joueur (prénom…) | es: Pedir un texto al jugador (nombre…) | de: Spieler nach einem Text fragen (Name…) | it: Chiedere un testo al giocatore (nome…) | pt: Pedir um texto ao jogador (nome…) | ru: Спросить текст у игрока (имя…) | zh: 让玩家输入文字（名字……） | ja: プレイヤーに文字を書いてもらう（名前…）

### Screen filters

- **Screen filter** → fr: Filtre d'écran | es: Filtro de pantalla | de: Bildschirmfilter | it: Filtro dello schermo | pt: Filtro de tela | ru: Фильтр экрана | zh: 屏幕滤镜 | ja: 画面フィルター
- **Stop the filter** → fr: Arrêter le filtre | es: Detener el filtro | de: Filter stoppen | it: Ferma il filtro | pt: Parar o filtro | ru: Остановить фильтр | zh: 停止滤镜 | ja: フィルターを止める

### Physics

- **Set the physics world** → fr: Régler le monde physique | es: Ajustar el mundo físico | de: Physikwelt einstellen | it: Regola il mondo fisico | pt: Ajustar o mundo físico | ru: Настроить физический мир | zh: 设置物理世界 | ja: 物理の世界を設定
- **Adjust a physics object** → fr: Régler un objet physique | es: Ajustar un objeto físico | de: Physik-Objekt einstellen | it: Regola un oggetto fisico | pt: Ajustar um objeto físico | ru: Настроить физический объект | zh: 设置物理物体 | ja: 物理オブジェクトを設定
- **Push (physics force)** → fr: Pousser (force physique) | es: Empujar (fuerza física) | de: Schieben (Physikkraft) | it: Spingere (forza fisica) | pt: Empurrar (força física) | ru: Толкать (физическая сила) | zh: 推动（物理力） | ja: 押す（物理の力）
- **Set the speed (physics)** → fr: Régler la vitesse (physique) | es: Ajustar la velocidad (física) | de: Tempo einstellen (Physik) | it: Regola la velocità (fisica) | pt: Ajustar a velocidade (física) | ru: Задать скорость (физика) | zh: 设置速度（物理） | ja: 速さを決める（物理）
- **Launch (angle and speed)** → fr: Lancer (angle et vitesse) | es: Lanzar (ángulo y velocidad) | de: Abwerfen (Winkel und Tempo) | it: Lancia (angolo e velocità) | pt: Lançar (ângulo e velocidade) | ru: Бросить (угол и скорость) | zh: 发射（角度和速度） | ja: 投げる（角度と速さ）
- **Explosion (physics blast)** → fr: Explosion (souffle physique) | es: Explosión (onda física) | de: Explosion (Druckwelle) | it: Esplosione (soffio fisico) | pt: Explosão (sopro físico) | ru: Взрыв (взрывная волна) | zh: 爆炸（物理冲击波） | ja: 爆発（ふきとばし）
- **Link two objects** → fr: Relier deux objets | es: Unir dos objetos | de: Zwei Objekte verbinden | it: Collega due oggetti | pt: Ligar dois objetos | ru: Соединить два объекта | zh: 连接两个物体 | ja: 2つのオブジェクトをつなぐ
- **Adjust a link** → fr: Régler une liaison | es: Ajustar una unión | de: Verbindung einstellen | it: Regola un collegamento | pt: Ajustar uma ligação | ru: Настроить связь | zh: 调整连接 | ja: つなぎを調整
- **Cut a link** → fr: Couper une liaison | es: Cortar una unión | de: Verbindung trennen | it: Taglia un collegamento | pt: Cortar uma ligação | ru: Разорвать связь | zh: 切断连接 | ja: つなぎを切る
- **Grab with the finger (physics)** → fr: Saisir avec le doigt (physique) | es: Agarrar con el dedo (física) | de: Mit dem Finger greifen (Physik) | it: Afferra con il dito (fisica) | pt: Agarrar com o dedo (física) | ru: Схватить пальцем (физика) | zh: 用手指抓取（物理） | ja: 指でつかむ（物理）
- **If the physics object…** → fr: Si l'objet physique… | es: Si el objeto físico… | de: Wenn das Physik-Objekt… | it: Se l'oggetto fisico… | pt: Se o objeto físico… | ru: Если физический объект… | zh: 如果物理物体… | ja: もし物理オブジェクトが…

## Node reference (English names)

### Events

- **On Start**: Runs only once, as soon as the scene starts. Example: place the enemies, show the starting score or start the music.
- **Every frame**: Runs over and over, on every frame of the game (about 60 times per second). Example: follow the finger or check a condition all the time. Avoid putting “Play music” or “Run one of my nodes” under it.
- **End of Click**: Runs when the player lifts their finger from the screen, anywhere. Example: stop shooting when the screen is released.
- **On Object Click** (Input: Object): Runs when the finger touches the chosen object. With a tag ("# card") as the target, it fires for every object with that tag: the touched object becomes the involved object. Example: a “Jump” button, opening a chest, picking an answer.
- **Object Released** (Input: Object): Runs when the finger is lifted above the chosen object. Example: confirm a button only when it is released.
- **Object Held Down** (Input: Object): Repeats on every frame as long as the finger stays on the chosen object. Example: left / right buttons: while you hold them, the character moves.
- **Finger held down**: Repeats on every frame as long as a finger is on the screen, anywhere. Example: make a ship climb while the screen is held (use doigt.x and doigt.y in formulas).
- **Back button pressed**: Runs when the player presses the Back button of their phone (arrow or swipe gesture). Great for opening a pause menu or going back to the previous screen. Without this node, the Back button does nothing during the game. Example: Back → “Pause the game”, then show a “Resume / Quit” menu.
- **On every new scene** [newer than 1.0.1142]: Runs every time a new scene opens. Made for the "Global logic" (which runs in every scene): for example, placing the chosen army on each map. In an ordinary scene, "On start" is enough.
- **Drag Start** (Input: Object): Runs when the player starts dragging the chosen object (it must be “Movable (draggable in Play mode)”). Example: enlarge a card when it is picked up.
- **Drag End** (Input: Object): Runs when the player drops the object they were dragging. Example: check whether a puzzle piece is in the right place.
- **Collision A/B** (Inputs: Object A, Object B): Runs once, when object A starts touching object B. They must separate before it can run again. This is also the event to use for “entering a zone”. Example: the player touches the finish zone → next level.
- **Exit Zone** (Inputs: Object A, Object B): Runs once, when object A stops touching object B (it leaves the zone). Example: close a door when the player walks away.
- **On Hover** (Input: Object): Runs when the finger, sliding across the screen, reaches the chosen object. Example: light up a button when the finger passes over it.
- **End of Hover** (Input: Object): Runs when the finger leaves the object it was over. Example: turn off a button's highlight.
- **On Impact (Physics)** (Input: Object): Runs when the chosen object (dynamic physics) lands on a floor or bounces. Example: play a landing sound or shake the camera.
- **When Variable Changes** (Input: Variable): Runs every time the value of the chosen variable changes. Example: when “vie” (health) changes, update the health bar.
- **Local Event** (Input: Event name): Your own event, with the name you choose. It is started by the “Call event” node in the same Blueprint. Example: a “GameOver” event called from several places.
- **On Action Click (Adventure)**: Runs when the player presses the scene's “BtnAction” object (action button). Example: talk to a character or open a door in an adventure game.
- **If object touches Tag** (Inputs: Object, Tag): Runs once per contact when the chosen object touches an object with this tag. The touched object becomes the “Implied Object”. The "Touched side" setting limits the event to one side of the object (top, bottom, left, right): "top of the object" means something comes down on it, for example an elevator crushing it. "Anywhere" (default) ignores the side. Example: the player touches a coin (tag “piece”) → destroy the involved object and add 1 to the score.

### Scene & HUD

- **Go to scene** (Input: Scene  →  Output: none (end of script)): Leaves the current scene and goes to the chosen scene. This node ends the script. Example: go to the “Well done!” screen after the last level.
- **Go to scene (by name)** (Input: Scene name  →  Output: none (end of script)): Goes to the scene whose name you type (or a formula giving that name). This node ends the script. Example: a formula like ="Level" + level to choose the level with a variable.
- **Next scene** (Output: none (end of script)): Goes to the scene placed just after in the scene list. This node ends the script. Example: the player reaches the finish → next level.
- **Previous scene** (Output: none (end of script)): Goes to the scene placed just before in the scene list. This node ends the script. Example: a “Back” button in a menu.
- **Restart the scene** (Output: none (end of script)): Restarts the scene from the beginning: objects back in place and local variables back to their starting value. Global variables do not change. Example: Game Over when health reaches 0.
- **Open a HUD** (Input: Scene): Shows another scene on top of the game, like a layer (HUD), with its own Blueprint. Example: a pause menu or an inventory.
- **Close the HUD**: Closes the open HUD. Example: the “Close” button of the pause menu.
- **Place a copy of a scene** (Inputs: Scene, X position, Y position): Places a copy of the chosen scene (prefab) in the game, at position X, Y. Example: spawn a group of enemies prepared in another scene.
- **Destroy the copies of a scene** (Input: Scene): Removes all copies of the chosen scene placed in the game. Example: clear all enemy groups at the end of a wave.
- **Quit the game** (Output: none (end of script)): Closes the exported game. In the editor, nothing closes: use the stop button. Example: a “Quit” button in the main menu.
- **Small message at the bottom of the screen** (Input: Message): Shows a small message at the bottom of the screen for a few seconds. Start with = to show a calculation. Example: ="Score: " + score
- **Write to the log (for debugging)** (Input: Message): Writes a message in the project log (diagnostic file), without showing anything in the game. Start with = to write a calculation. Example: ="health = " + vie, to check a value while testing.
- **Follow with camera** (Inputs: Object, Follow X (yes / no), Follow Y (yes / no), Parallax X only (yes / no), Object lower on screen (pixels, 0 = centre, 300 = towards the bottom), Object further right on screen (pixels, 0 = centre, negative = left)): The camera follows the chosen object. You can make it follow only horizontally or vertically. With no object, the camera stops following. Example: follow the player through a big platform level.
- **Camera limits** (Inputs: Minimum X (left edge of the level), Maximum X (right edge), Minimum Y (top), Maximum Y (bottom; all 0 = no limits)): Keeps the camera inside the level edges: it never shows the empty space beyond. All 0 = no limits. Example: a level 6480 pixels wide: minimum X 0, maximum X 6480, minimum Y 0, maximum Y 1080, with “Follow with camera” on the player.
- **Scroll the camera with a finger** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: On (yes / no), Scroll sideways (yes / no), Scroll up and down (yes / no)): Turns finger scrolling on (or off): dragging in the scene moves the camera. A simple tap is still a tap (a tower, a button). HUD buttons never scroll. The camera stays inside the limits set with “Camera limits”. Example: On start: Camera limits (0, 3840, 0, 1080), then Scroll the camera with a finger: the player drags a map two screens wide.
- **Camera smoothing** (Input: Follow speed (0.01 to 1)): Sets how fast the camera catches up with the followed object: 0.01 = very soft, 1 = stuck to the object. Example: 0.1 for a smooth camera that follows with a slight delay.
- **Screen flash** (Inputs: Color, Intensity (%, 0 = none), Duration (seconds)): Flashes a color over the whole screen, fading out in a moment (intensity in %, duration in seconds). Example: a 0.5-second red flash when the player is hit.
- **Screen tint** (Inputs: Color, Intensity (%, 0 = none), Transition (seconds)): Lays a color over the whole game (under the HUD), with a smooth transition. Intensity 0 removes it. Example: night falls: dark blue, intensity 55, 2-second transition.
- **Vignette** (Inputs: Color, Intensity (%, 0 = none), Transition (seconds)): Gently darkens the edges of the screen, like in a movie (under the HUD). Intensity 0 removes it. Example: a scary mood in a cave: intensity 75.
- **Screen fade** (Inputs: Direction, Color, Duration (seconds)): Fades the whole screen out to a color, or back in from it. The fade carries over from one scene to the next. Example: “Screen fade” (fade out), “Wait” 1 second, “Go to scene”, then “Screen fade” (fade in) when the next level starts.
- **Atmosphere (rain, snow, night…)** (Inputs: What falls or floats, Light, Strength, Ambient sounds (rain, wind, thunder…), Appears over (seconds)): Puts an atmosphere over the whole screen that stays until the next Atmosphere node: what falls or floats (rain, storm with lightning, snow, petals, leaves, fireflies, hearts, bubbles, mist) and a light (night, sunset, memory, dream, fear, dark). The old one fades out while the new one comes in. Example: after the "Leave" choice, storm and night light; "none" and "normal" remove everything.
- **Zoom the screen** (Inputs: Zoom (%, 100 = normal), Towards, Duration (seconds)): Smoothly enlarges the whole game screen (the scene, or a story's background and characters) towards the center, the face, a side, the top or the bottom. 100 = back to normal; the dialogue box and the HUD don't move. Example: zoom 140 towards the face for 2 seconds when Hana is scared, then zoom 100.
- **Darkness and light mood** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Color of the night, Darkness (%, 0 = full day, 100 = almost pitch black), Changes over (seconds: 30 = a real sunset)): Darkens the whole game (under the buttons and score) with the color you choose. Darkness 0 = full daylight, 100 = pitch black, except around light sources. The level and the color change smoothly: over 30 seconds you go from day to an orange dusk and then a blue night, like a sunset. Example: a sunset: “Darkness and light mood” orange, darkness 40, over 6 seconds; “Wait” 6 seconds; then “Darkness and light mood” night blue, darkness 90, over 6 seconds.
- **Day and night cycle** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Length of a full day (seconds, 0 = stop), We start at…, Repeat forever (yes) or one day only (no)): Takes the whole game from day to an orange evening, a blue night, dawn, then day again, all by itself. You choose the length of a full day (30 to 120 seconds for a lively game), the starting moment and whether the cycle repeats forever. A paused game freezes the cycle. Length 0 = stop the cycle (the sky stays as it is). A manual setting with “Darkness and light mood” takes over. Your lights (“Light source (torch, lantern…)”) stay on: you see them better at night. Example: a living world: on start, “Day and night cycle” with a length of 90 seconds, starting “Full day”, looping.
- **Camera shake** (Inputs: Strength, Duration (milliseconds, 1000 = 1 s)): Shakes the screen with the chosen strength and duration (in milliseconds). Example: an explosion: intensity 15, duration 400.
- **Vibration** (Input: Duration (milliseconds, 1000 = 1 s)): Makes the phone vibrate for the chosen duration (in milliseconds). Without a vibration motor, nothing happens. Example: 100 ms when the player gets hit.
- **Save state**: Remembers the state of the scene (objects and variables) and the global variables, like a save point. Example: a checkpoint flag in the middle of the level.
- **Restore state**: Puts the scene back as it was at the last “Save state”. If there is no save yet, nothing changes. Example: start again from the checkpoint after a fall.
- **Save variables to a file** (Inputs: Save name, Variables (empty = all)): Writes the values of your variables (global ones and the scene's) to a file on the device, so they are still there when the player closes and reopens the game. “Save name” lets you keep several games. Leave “Variables” empty to keep everything, or type names separated by commas (score, lives). Unlike “Save state”, it survives closing the game. Example: When the player scores: “Add to Variable” on “score”, then “Save variables to a file”. The score is written to the file at every point.
- **Load variables from a file** (Inputs: Save name, Variables (empty = all)  →  Outputs: Loaded / No save found): Brings back the values written by “Save variables to a file” (same save name). Every variable that still exists gets its saved value back. Output “Loaded” when it worked, “No save found” on the very first game. Often placed right after “At start”. Example: Right after “On Start”: “Load variables from a file”, then “Set a property” to show the score that was found.

### Time

- **Wait** (Input: Duration (seconds)): Waits for the chosen time, in seconds, then continues. The rest of the game keeps running during the wait. Example: show “You lose!”, wait 2 seconds, then restart the scene.
- **Repeat** (Inputs: Every (seconds), Number of times (0 = endless), Timer name (optional)  →  Outputs: Right away / Each time / Move finished): Runs the “Each time” output every X seconds, a number of times (0 = forever), then “Move finished”. “Right away” runs at the start. If it is already running, it does not start again. Example: spawn an enemy every 3 seconds.
- **Countdown** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Start value (optional), Timer name (optional)  →  Outputs: Every second / Move finished): Removes 1 from the chosen variable (a number) every second until 0. “Every second” runs on each tick, “Move finished” at 0. “Start value (optional)” sets the starting value. Example: a 60-second timer: at 0, Game Over.
- **Stop a timer** (Input: Timer name (empty = all)): Stops the timer (Repeat or Countdown) with this name, or all timers if the name is empty. Example: stop the timer when the player wins.
- **Game speed (slow motion)** (Input: Speed (1 = normal, 0.5 = slow)): Changes the speed of the whole game: 1 = normal, 0.5 = slow motion, 2 = fast (from 0 to 4). Example: a slow-motion effect for 2 seconds.
- **Pause the game**: Pauses the game: movements and timers stop. Example: open the pause menu.
- **Resume the game**: Resumes the game after a pause. Example: the “Continue” button of the pause menu.
- **Hit stop** (Inputs: Duration (seconds), Speed during the stop (0 = frozen)): Slows the whole game almost to a stop for a very short moment (in real seconds), then the game goes back to its speed. It gives “punch” to impacts. Example: when an enemy explodes: duration 0.06, speed 0.05.

### Appearance & Objects

- **Move Object** (Inputs: Object, X, Y): Puts the object directly at position X, Y (teleport). Example: put the player back at the start.
- **Push object** (Inputs: Object, Add X, Add Y): Moves the object by the given distance from where it is now. A physics object is stopped by walls. Example: linked to “Object Held Down”: “Add X” = 5 moves right.
- **Set a property** (Inputs: Object, Property, Value): Changes an object property chosen from a list (x, y, rotation, opacity, text…). Example: set the rotation of a clock hand to =temps * 90.
- **Rotation** (Inputs: Object, Angle (degrees)): Turns the object to the given angle, in degrees. Example: =wheel.rotation + 5 linked to “Every frame” keeps the object “wheel” spinning.
- **Transparency** (Inputs: Object, Opacity (0 to 1)): Sets the object's transparency: 0 = invisible, 1 = solid. Example: 0.5 for a half-transparent ghost.
- **Visibility** (Inputs: Object, Visible (yes / no)): Shows (true) or hides (false) the object. Example: show a “You win!” message hidden at the start.
- **Give a tag (object family)** (Inputs: Object, Tag): Gives the object a new tag (label). Example: a defeated enemy gets the tag “harmless”.
- **Bring to front / send back** (Inputs: Object, Depth (bigger = in front)): Changes the object's layer: the bigger the number, the more the object is in front of others. Example: put the player in front of a decoration.
- **Grow / shrink** (Inputs: Object, Horizontal size (1 = normal), Vertical size (1 = normal)): Changes the object's size: 1 = normal, 2 = twice as big, 0.5 = half. Example: the player grows after eating a mushroom.
- **Destroy Object** (Input: Object): Removes the chosen object from the scene. Example: choose “Implied Object” to destroy the coin the player just touched.
- **Destroy by Tag** (Input: Tag to destroy): Removes all objects with this tag. Example: a bomb destroys every “Enemy” object.
- **Change Image** (Inputs: Object, Image): Replaces the object's image with another image from the Assets. Empty = no image. Example: the character looks left or right depending on the button.
- **Modify Color** (Inputs: Object, Color): Changes the object's color. Example: a button turns green when the answer is right.
- **Generate clone (Spawner)** (Inputs: Object A, Object B): Creates a copy of object B (the model) at the place of object A (the spawn point). Example: a cannon (A) that spawns cannonballs (B).
- **Color Filter** (Inputs: Object, Filter): Applies a filter to the object: Black and White, Sepia, Invert, or None to remove it. Example: switch to black and white during a flashback.
- **Color blending (light effect)** (Inputs: Object, Filter): Changes how the object blends with what is behind it (Additive, Multiply, Screen, Invert). Example: Additive for a glowing light or flame.
- **Mirror Effect / Invert** (Inputs: Object, Axis): Flips the object: Horizontal (left / right) or Vertical (up / down). Example: the character faces the way it walks.
- **Lock / unlock the object** (Inputs: Object, Locked (yes / no)): Locks or unlocks the object in the editor (the padlock). It has no effect during the game: to stop an object from being dragged, use “Change the behavior”.
- **Background scrolling (depth)** (Inputs: Object, Background speed (1 = normal, 0.5 = slower, far away effect)): Sets how fast the object scrolls when the camera moves: 1 = normal, 0.5 = half as fast (depth effect). Example: mountains in the background that scroll slowly.
- **Link two objects** (Inputs: Object A, Object B): Attaches object A (the child) to object B (the parent): A follows B when it moves. Example: a sword that follows the character's hand.
- **Glowing halo** (Inputs: Object, State, Color, Glow size): Surrounds the object with a soft glow of the chosen color and size (it follows the shape of images), or removes it. Example: a bonus that glows yellow, size 20.
- **Particle effect** (Inputs: Object, Preset, Count (0 = preset's), Color (empty = preset's), Size (1 = normal), Image (empty = preset shapes)): Fires a burst of particles on the object: explosion, sparks, dust, smoke, fire, rain, snow, confetti, trail, wake trail, hyperspace or speed lines. Count, color and size can be set. With an image ("Image" setting), each particle becomes that image: a drawn explosion, a star, a leaf… Example: a hit enemy explodes in magenta: Explosion preset, color #FF40D0.
- **Particles on / off** (Inputs: Object, State): Turns a “Particles” object on or off: it emits continuously or stops (particles already fired finish their life). Example: turn the engine exhaust on when the ship moves.
- **Particle burst** (Inputs: Object, Number of particles): Fires many particles at once from a “Particles” object, with its settings (preset, color, size). Example: 80 confetti when the level is won.
- **Change particle preset** (Inputs: Object, Preset): Changes the preset of a “Particles” object during the game. Example: a fire that turns into smoke when it is put out.
- **Blink** (Inputs: Object, State, Speed (milliseconds, 1000 = 1 s), Duration (milliseconds, 0 = endless)): Makes the object blink at the chosen speed (ms), for a duration (ms, 0 = forever), or stops the blinking. Example: the player blinks for 1 second after being hit.
- **Create a copy of the object** (Inputs: Object B, X position, Y position): Creates a copy of object B (the model) at position X, Y. The copy becomes the “Implied Object”. Example: drop a rock at a random position: X = random(0, 800).
- **Shoot an object** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Model name, Direction, Speed, Destroy off screen (yes / no), Shot lifetime (seconds, 0 = unlimited)): Creates a projectile (the object named in “Model name”) at object A, and launches it at the chosen speed: 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, towards object B (“Toward target”) or along A's angle. Example: a ship firing lasers upwards (270).
- **Launch a guided missile (curve)** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Model name (image facing right), Starting direction (0 = right, 90 = down, 180 = left, 270 = up), Speed, Turn: degrees per step (small = wide curve), Wait before aiming (seconds), Lifetime (seconds, 0 = endless)): Launches a missile that starts in one direction, then slowly turns toward its target: it follows a real curve. “Object A” is the one that fires, “Object B” is the target to follow. The model is a hidden object whose image faces right. A small “Turn” gives a wide curve; when its lifetime ends, a missile that hit nothing explodes. Example: an enemy fires a missile at the ship: object A = the enemy, object B = the ship, lifetime 3 seconds.
- **Destroy the object after a delay (seconds)** (Inputs: Object, Delay (seconds)): Removes the chosen object after a delay (in seconds). Handy to make an explosion disappear once its animation is over. Example: after “Generate clone (Spawner)” and “Play animation”, the explosion image is destroyed 0.4 seconds later.
- **Team colour (replaces the pink in the drawing)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Team colour, Colour to replace in the drawing (pink by default), Tolerance (1 to 100): higher also replaces similar colours, Shades replaced (1 to 100): 100 = every shade of this hue, small = only the exact marker colour): One drawing for all teams: paint the parts to colour (cloak, flag, plume) with a marker colour (bright pink #FF00FF by default), then this node replaces that pink with the team colour for the object. The drawing's shadows and highlights are kept (a dark pink becomes a dark blue). Tolerance says how far a colour may stray from the marker and still be replaced. Nothing is changed in the images: it all happens at display time, so do it again at the start of each game. Example: two armies with the same images: player in blue, enemy in red.
- **Set Progress** (Inputs: Object, New progress): Sets how full a progress bar is, between its minimum and maximum. Example: “New progress” = vie (health), for a health bar.
- **Screen wrap** (Input: Object): Whatever leaves one side of the screen comes back on the opposite side (Pac-Man effect). Example: an asteroid that leaves on the right and comes back on the left.
- **Clamp to screen** (Inputs: Object, Margin): Stops the object from leaving the screen. The margin stops it a little before the edge. Example: the player's ship always stays visible.
- **Electrocution** (Inputs: Object, Lightning color, Duration (seconds, 0 = endless), Intensity (0 = stop, 1 to 3)): Lightning crackles around the object: it flashes in the lightning color, shakes and throws sparks. Duration 0 = endless (electric fence); intensity 0 = stop. Example: the wizard touches a trap: “Electrocution” on the wizard (1 second), “Wait” 1 second, then “Restart the scene”.
- **Light source (torch, lantern…)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Light color, Radius (pixels: distance from the light's center), Lighting (%, 100 = normal, 200 = very strong), Colored glow (%, 0 = none, 200 = very strong), Flicker, Switching on, Horizontal shift (pixels), Vertical shift (pixels, negative = up)): Attaches a light to the object: it follows the object when it moves (a character's torch, a lantern, a fire…), even if the object is the child of another. Settings: color, radius in pixels (distance from the center), lighting (100 = normal, up to 300: stronger and farther), colored glow (0 = none), flicker (none, candle, torch, flickers) and shift. One light per object, 8 at most at once. It cuts through the darkness set by “Darkness and light mood”; without darkness it only adds its glow. “Switching on” setting: “Only when it is dark” turns the light on by itself at nightfall (ideal with “Day and night cycle”). Example: a character's torch: placed on a “lantern” object that is a child of the hero, radius 360, flicker “torch”.
- **Turn off the object's light** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Input: Object): Turns off the light attached to the object. To turn it back on, use “Light source (torch, lantern…)” again. Example: a “Lantern” button turns off the hero's light.
- **Shadow under the object** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Shadow, Shadow strength (%), Shadow width (% of the object), Vertical shift (pixels, negative = up)): Puts a soft shadow under the object (or removes it with “No”). It follows the object when it moves; you can set its strength and width. It instantly gives volume to characters standing on a backdrop. You can also tick the “Shadow under the object” box in the Inspector, with no node at all. Example: a shadow under the hero: strength 50, width 70.
- **Object trail** (Inputs: Object, Preset, Color (empty = preset's), Size (1 = normal)): The object leaves a trail of particles behind it when it moves (preset, color and size of your choice). Set on a shot's model, every shot inherits it. Preset “None” removes it. Example: shots that leave a glowing trail: target = the shot's model, Trail preset.
- **Create object** (Inputs: Object, X position, Y position): Creates a copy of the chosen object (the model) at position X, Y. Example: add a crate at an exact spot.
- **Fade** (Inputs: Object, Target opacity (0 to 1), Duration (seconds)): Smoothly changes the object's opacity to the target value, over the chosen time (seconds). The next nodes run without waiting. Example: fade out a title in 1 second (target opacity 0).

### Variables & Inventory

- **Modify Variable** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Value): Gives the variable a new value (a number, a text, yes / no or a calculation). Example: set “score” back to 0.
- **Add to Variable** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Value to add, Back to 0 after (optional)): Adds the value to the variable (a negative number subtracts). For a text variable, adds the text at the end. With "Back to 0 after", the variable turns like a counter: after 9 it goes back to 0 (and below 0 it goes to 9). Example: score + 1 for each coin; a padlock digit: + 1 on each tap, back to 0 after 9.
- **Keep a variable between two values** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Minimum, Maximum): Keeps the variable (a number) between a minimum and a maximum. Example: health never goes above 100.
- **Random number** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Between (min, max)): Puts a random number in the variable. random(1, 6) gives a number from 1 to 6. Example: a dice roll.
- **Add to inventory** (Inputs: Object, Variable): Puts the object in the inventory (a variable of type Inventory List). It is only added once. Example: pick up a key.
- **Remove from inventory** (Inputs: Object, Variable): Removes the object from the inventory. Example: use the key to open the door.
- **If in inventory** (Inputs: Object, Variable  →  Outputs: True / False / Then): Follows the True output if the object is in the inventory, False otherwise. Example: the door only opens if the key is in the inventory.
- **Combine two objects** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Result object name): Replaces objects A and B with a copy of the object whose name you type, at A's place. If that model does not exist, nothing changes. Example: stick + cloth = torch.

### Logic & Conditions

- **Condition** (Input: Condition  →  Outputs: True / False / Then): Tests a condition: follows the True output if it is right, False otherwise. “Then” runs afterwards, in both cases. Example: score >= 10 → True → next scene.
- **If joystick** (Outputs: Up / Down / Left / Right / Idle / Then): Follows the output matching the joystick direction: Up, Down, Left, Right, or Idle when it is not touched. Example: linked to “Every frame” to play the walking animation in the right direction.
- **If on ground** (Input: Object  →  Outputs: True / False / Then): True if the bottom of the object is standing on a fixed, visible object (floor, platform), False otherwise. Example: only allow jumping when the player is on the ground.
- **If moving** (Input: Object  →  Outputs: True / False / Then): True if the object moved since the previous frame, False otherwise. Example: play the walking animation only when the character moves.
- **Run one of my nodes** (Input: Function): Runs one of your nodes (a Blueprint made in the My nodes section), then continues. If it has settings, a line appears for each. Do not put it under “Every frame”. Example: a “LoseLife” node used by several enemies.
- **Call event** (Input: Event name): Runs the “Local Event” with this name, in the same Blueprint, then continues. Example: call “GameOver” from the fall and from the timer.
- **Sequence** (Outputs: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4): Runs its outputs one after the other: 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. An output with no link is skipped. Example: at start: 1 = place the player, 2 = start the music, 3 = show the score.
- **Cooldown** (Inputs: Object, Delay (seconds)  →  Outputs: Ready / Not yet): Lets things through “Ready” at most once per delay (in seconds); otherwise it is “Not yet”. With an object chosen, each object has its own delay. Example: shoot at most once every 0.5 second.
- **If off-screen** (Inputs: Object, Margin (pixels)  →  Outputs: True / False / Then): True if the object is completely off the screen (plus the margin), False otherwise. Example: destroy bullets that leave the screen.
- **If / Else** (Inputs: If (condition), Else if (condition)  →  Outputs: If / Else if / Else / Then): Tests the first condition, then the second: follows “If”, “Else if” or “Else”. “Then” runs afterwards. Example: if score >= 100 → gold, else if score >= 50 → silver, else → bronze.
- **By value** (Inputs: Value to test, Case 1, Case 2, Case 3, Case 4, Case 5, Case 6  →  Outputs: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / None / Then): Compares the value to test with cases 1 to 6 and follows the output of the first matching case; “None” if nothing matches. An empty case is skipped. Example: depending on “weapon”: 1 = sword, 2 = bow, 3 = wand.

### Texts & Dialogues

- **Modify Text** (Inputs: Object, New text): Replaces the text of a Text object. Start with = to show a calculation. Example: ="Score: " + score
- **Show dialogue** (Inputs: Object, Sentence name (in the game texts)): Writes into the Text object the sentence matching the key, from the dialogue file (dialogues.txt). Several languages: write “hello.en = Hello”, “hello.fr = Bonjour”…; the game uses the language in the “langue” variable, otherwise the phone language. “\n” = new line. Example: the key “hello_merchant” shows the merchant's line.
- **Append to text** (Inputs: Object, Variable, Text to add): Adds text at the end of a variable of type Text. Example: type a password letter by letter.

### Movements & AI

- **Play movement (steps)** (Inputs: Object, Movement name): Plays on the object a movement made in Assets → Movement (steps: position, rotation, size, transparency). The engine computes everything in between. While it moves, the object's gravity and controls are switched off. The next nodes run without waiting. Example: a platform that goes up and down in a loop, or a sliding door.
- **Stop the movement** (Input: Object): Stops the movement running on the object. It stays where it is. Example: stop the platform when the player presses a button.
- **Spin the object continuously** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Spin speed (degrees per second, negative = other way, 0 = stop)): Makes the object spin on itself without stopping, at the speed you choose in degrees per second. A negative number spins the other way, 0 stops the rotation. The movement follows game time: it stops while the game is paused. Example: A spinning saw: "At start" → this node on the saw, speed 360.
- **Follow the path** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Path name, Speed (pixels per second), Turn to face the way it goes (yes / no), Random side offset (pixels, ±: each one walks in its own lane), Avoid the others: step aside to avoid overlapping and overtake slower ones (yes / no), Usable width to step aside (pixels on each side of the road centre), Image angle (0 = faces right, 90 = faces down)  →  Outputs: Right away / Arrived): Makes the object follow a path drawn with the “Path” tool in Assets: it is placed on the starting point, then moves from point to point at the chosen speed. At a crossroads it picks its exit as you set it (random, take turns, by a variable). The “Reached the end” exit fires when it reaches a point with no exit. With “Random side offset”, each object walks in its own lane (random shift): several enemies advance side by side instead of overlapping. With “Avoid the others”, an object that catches up with a slower one steps aside, overtakes it and returns to its lane; if the road is too narrow, it follows instead. Example: An enemy appears: Follow the path “Enemy_path”, speed 150. “Reached the end” exit → Deal damage to the base, then Destroy the object.
- **Stop following the path** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Input: Object): Stops the object where it is: it no longer follows its path (the “Reached the end” exit will not fire). Example: An enemy is frozen by a trap: Stop the path, then later Follow the path again so it moves on.
- **Stop the object** (Input: Object): Stops the object dead: no more speed, push, jump or automatic movement. Example: freeze an enemy hit by an ice spell.
- **Stop movements** (Input: Object): Turns off the object's automatic movements: move continuously, pursue and flee. Example: the enemy stops chasing when the player hides.
- **Move forward continuously** (Inputs: Object, Speed): The object moves by itself, in the direction it is facing, at the chosen speed. Example: a bullet or a moving car.
- **Go to an object (path)** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Speed, Diagonals (yes / no), Stop, These tags block the path (other units, separated by commas), Stay in the shown zone (the path never leaves the range), Name of the zone to respect (empty = the unnamed zone)  →  Outputs: Right away / Arrived): Object A goes to object B, finding the shortest path by itself, square by square, without going through walls ("Solid" tiles of a tile layer, fixed physical objects). The path is updated when B moves. “Arrived” runs when A touches B. The "Stop" setting lets the object stop on a neighbouring cell, well centered (grid games); "These tags block the path" makes it go around other units. In the advanced settings, “Stay in the shown zone” limits the path to the cells shown by “Show reachable cells”: the object never walks through a cell outside its range. Example: a ghost chasing the player through a maze.
- **Go to a point (path)** (Inputs: Object, X position, Y position, Speed, Diagonals (yes / no), These tags block the path (other units, separated by commas), Stay in the shown zone (the path never leaves the range), Name of the zone to respect (empty = the unnamed zone)  →  Outputs: Right away / Arrived): Object A goes to point X, Y around the walls, by the shortest path (square by square). With =doigt.x and =doigt.y, it goes where the screen is touched. “Arrived” runs on arrival. If there is no path, it stays where it is. In the advanced settings, “Stay in the shown zone” limits the path to the cells shown by “Show reachable cells”: the object never walks through a cell outside its range. Example: tap a square to send the hero there, in a strategy game or a dungeon.
- **Stop the path** (Input: Object): The object stops following its path (“Go to an object (path)” or “Go to a point (path)”) and stays where it is. Example: the fly stops when the game is won.
- **Place on a cell (column, row)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Column (0 = the first), Row (0 = the first)): Puts object A exactly in the middle of the chosen cell (column and row, counted from 0 at the top left). The grid is the one of the scene's tile map. With the 🔗 button, plug in “Touched column” and “Touched row” to send it to the cell the finger touches. Example: move a piece to the touched cell in a board game.
- **Center on its cell** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Input: Object): Object A stays in its cell but goes back exactly to the middle. Handy when a move stopped between two cells. Example: re-center a hero after its move.
- **Go to the cell (path)** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Column, Row, Speed, Diagonals (yes / no), These tags block the path (other units, separated by commas), Stay in the shown zone (the path never leaves the range), Name of the zone to respect (empty = the unnamed zone)  →  Outputs: Right away / Arrived): The object walks to the CENTER of the cell (column, row), going around walls, blocking terrains and the units with the given tags. Default: the cell touched by the finger. "Arrived" output once on the cell. In the advanced settings, “Stay in the shown zone” limits the path to the cells shown by “Show reachable cells”: the object never walks through a cell outside its range. Example: send a hero to a touched blue cell.
- **Move the piece one cell** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Inputs: Object, Direction, Speed, These tags block the path (other units, separated by commas)  →  Outputs: Arrived / Blocked (wall, terrain, unit, edge)): Moves the piece one cell (up, down, left, right), well centered. If the cell is a wall, a blocking terrain, a unit (tags) or the edge of the map: "Blocked" output. Otherwise "Arrived" at the end of the step. Example: move a board-game piece with ◀ ▶ ▲ ▼ buttons.
- **Chase an object** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Speed): Object A moves by itself towards object B, at the chosen speed. Example: a ghost following the player.
- **Flee an object** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Speed): Object A moves by itself away from object B, at the chosen speed. Example: a chicken running away from the player.
- **Push at an angle** (Inputs: Object, Angle (0 = right, 90 = down), Force): Pushes the object in a direction (in degrees: 0 = right, 90 = down, 180 = left, 270 = up) with the chosen force. Example: a spring that sends the player diagonally.
- **Impulse (jump)** (Inputs: Object, Vertical force (negative = up)): Launches the object upwards (negative number) or downwards (positive), and gives it physics so it falls back. Example: a jump: force -15.
- **Change the behavior** (Inputs: Object, How it moves, Speed, Jump height, Is a ladder, Collectable): Changes what the object does during the game, with the same choices as the Inspector's "Object behavior" window: Scenery, Ground / wall, Falls and bounces, Platform character, Patrol (back and forth), Top-down character, Dragged with a finger. You can also change the speed, the jump height, "is a ladder" and "collectable". Every setting left on "(don't change)" keeps its value. Example: a crate standing still (Ground / wall) starts to fall when a lever is pulled: Change the behavior → Falls and bounces.
- **Bounce around** (Inputs: Object, Strength (0 = stop), Duration (milliseconds, 1000 = 1 s), Keep going while moving (yes / no)): Makes the object hop (a small visual bounce) with the chosen intensity and duration. 0 stops it. It can keep going while the object moves. Example: a character that hops as it walks.
- **Face towards** (Inputs: Object A, Object B, Angle offset (degrees)): Turns object A towards object B. The offset fixes the image's direction (0 = the image faces right). Example: a turret aiming at the player.
- **Glide to** (Inputs: Object, X position, Y position, Duration (seconds)): Smoothly moves the object to position X, Y over the chosen time (seconds). The next nodes run without waiting. Example: a moving platform or a menu sliding onto the screen.

### Grids and puzzles

- **Go to the next turn** [newer than 1.0.1142] (Input: Teams, in order (tags separated by a comma)): Passes the game to the next team. Write the teams in order using their tags (e.g. player,enemy).
